setting: Liggins Institute, University of Auckland (review base)
population_detail: neonates at risk of hypoglycaemia across included studies
intervention: point-of-care glucose device methodologies (GO/GDH/HK x photometry/electrochemistry)
outcomes_measured: sensitivity and specificity of POC methods vs laboratory reference
primary_result: HK+electrochemistry most accurate; all methods specificity >=93%
effect_size: not a single pooled effect size (hierarchical random-effects diagnostic accuracy model)
secondary_results: GO+electrochemistry, GDH+electrochemistry, HK+electrochemistry showed superior sensitivity to photometric methods
ascertainment_method: QUADAS-2
directness: direct - spans multiple neonatal populations
grade_reason: imprecision (HK+electrochemistry stratum only 2 studies); indirectness (pooled across heterogeneous reference standards/populations)
funding: NIH and non-US-government support (per PubMed record)
key_limitation: limited studies using best-performing HK+electrochemistry method
notes: PROSPERO CRD42023488539; excluded CGM and pre-1990 studies; the key modern SR for Domain B
gestational_age_range: mixed (all neonatal GAs across included studies)
glucose_threshold_used: not a single threshold (accuracy review across chemistries)
dose_response_reported: not applicable (accuracy review, not outcome study)

population_detail: infants <30 days of age; hematocrit 23-70%
intervention: modified quinoprotein-resistant glucose dehydrogenase POC chemistry (ACCU-CHEK Inform II/Performa/Aviva)
outcomes_measured: correlation and ROC accuracy for detecting hypoglycaemia
primary_result: meter=0.99xreference+0.04; r2=0.976
effect_size: not applicable (regression)
secondary_results: 100% sensitivity for lab <2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL) when meter reading <2.8 mmol/L (50 mg/dL); AUC 0.993; weak hematocrit dependence outside typical neonatal range (45-70%)
ascertainment_method: paired POC meter vs hexokinase lab reference
directness: direct - neonatal population across 3 US centres
grade_reason: imprecision (single device family); indirectness (hematocrit effect analysis pooled across full 23-70% range not just neonatal-typical)
key_limitation: single device chemistry family tested
notes: Establishes 2.8 mmol/L (50 mg/dL) POC cutoff giving 100% sensitivity for this device
gestational_age_range: <30 days of age (mixed GA)
glucose_threshold_used: 2.2 mmol/L / 40 mg/dL (lab reference for hypoglycaemia)

population_detail: infants at risk for neonatal hypoglycaemia with initial low POC glucose
intervention: StatStrip (SS) and SureStep Flexx (SF) glucose meters
outcomes_measured: sensitivity/NPV of POC devices at 2.8 mmol/L cutoff; effect of bilirubin/hematocrit
primary_result: SS sensitivity 94.7% NPV 86.1%; SF sensitivity 100% NPV 100% at 2.8 mmol/L (50 mg/dL) cutoff
effect_size: mean glucose difference SS 0.21 (SD 0.70) mmol/L; SF -0.04 (SD 0.78) mmol/L
secondary_results: no correlation between mean glucose differences and hematocrit or bilirubin for either device
ascertainment_method: paired POC vs plasma glucose
directness: direct - at-risk neonates during high-risk screening period
grade_reason: imprecision (172 samples, single centre); indirectness (both devices already flagged as limited screening-only tools by the authors themselves)
key_limitation: authors conclude both devices have limited use compared to plasma glucose
notes: Companion/related group to Ngerncham 2011 (same Thai group testing same device pair with different cutoff)
gestational_age_range: 1-24 hours of life (at-risk neonates)
glucose_threshold_used: 2.8 mmol/L / 50 mg/dL (device cutoff tested)

population_detail: high-risk neonates aged 1-24 hours
intervention: Nova StatStrip and SureStep glucometers
outcomes_measured: sensitivity/specificity/NPV; cutoff for no-confirmation-needed
primary_result: StatStrip sensitivity 62% specificity 100%; SureStep sensitivity 53.3% specificity 100%
effect_size: mean differences 11.2 (SD 8.4) mg/dL (StatStrip); 13.7 (SD 6.8) mg/dL (SureStep)
secondary_results: cutoffs with 100% NPV: 63 mg/dL (3.5 mmol/L) StatStrip, 62 mg/dL (3.4 mmol/L) SureStep; both devices read higher than lab on average
ascertainment_method: paired POC vs plasma glucose
directness: direct - high-risk neonates, first 24h
grade_reason: imprecision (single centre, 166 neonates); risk of bias (glucometer cutoffs derived and tested in the same sample - not externally validated)
key_limitation: explicit conclusion: neither glucometer has sufficient validity to replace laboratory testing; confirmatory testing needed for POC readings 39-63 mg/dL (StatStrip) and 39-62 mg/dL (SureStep)
notes: Derives a materially HIGHER confirmation cutoff (~3.5 mmol/L/63 mg/dL) than BAPM's operative 2.6 mmol/L/47 mg/dL - direct evidence for the (d) tension on confirm-below-X
gestational_age_range: 1-24 hours of life (high-risk neonates)
glucose_threshold_used: 63 mg/dL / 3.5 mmol/L (StatStrip) and 62 mg/dL / 3.4 mmol/L (SureStep) - proposed confirmation cutoffs

population_detail: newborn infants requiring bedside glucose testing
intervention: three POCT systems: Elite XL; Ascensia Contour; ABL 735 blood gas analyser
outcomes_measured: agreement with ISO 15197 accuracy criteria
primary_result: none of the three POCT systems met ISO 15197 accuracy criteria
effect_size: not a single pooled effect size (device comparison study)
secondary_results: all three systems tended to OVERESTIMATE glycaemia; Contour showed important inaccuracy with increasing haematocrit; ABL 735 (blood gas) most accurate but requires >15x more blood volume than handheld glucometers
ascertainment_method: paired POC/blood-gas vs central lab hexokinase
directness: direct - newborn infant population
grade_reason: risk of bias (retrospective, single centre); inconsistency (all 3 systems failed ISO 15197 - a negative finding for the whole class of devices tested)
key_limitation: none of the 3 tested systems met the accuracy standard applied
notes: Systematic OVERESTIMATION - contrasts with Parikh 2025's later finding of systematic underestimation with a different device/era, illustrating inconsistent bias direction across studies (see synthesis d)
gestational_age_range: newborn infants (GA not further specified in abstract)
glucose_threshold_used: not a single threshold (accuracy study vs ISO 15197 criteria)
glucose_measurement_method: point-of-care and blood gas vs laboratory (hexokinase)

setting: Women's College Hospital, University of Toronto
population_detail: NICU infants undergoing heel-stick glucose testing
intervention: Ames Glucometer Elite electrochemical glucose meter
outcomes_measured: regression agreement; detection of Lo (hypoglycaemic) readings
primary_result: r=0.93; Sy/x=0.59 mmol/L (reduced to 0.45 with on-ice delivery)
effect_size: intercept 0.47 +/- 0.14 mmol/L (1 SEM)
secondary_results: 29/30 samples read as Lo by Elite were <2.2 mmol/L on CX7 (only 1 was exactly 2.2 mmol/L); imprecision <5% CV at all tested levels
ascertainment_method: paired heel-stick POC vs central lab
directness: direct - NICU population
grade_reason: imprecision (single-centre, single device); indirectness (pre-dates modern electrochemical hexokinase/GDH devices by 15+ years)
key_limitation: classic early evidence; on-ice sample delivery reduced discordance from 24% to 8%

gestational_age_range: NICU infants (GA not specified)
glucose_threshold_used: 2.2 mmol/L / 40 mg/dL (reference hypoglycaemia threshold used for detection analysis)

population_detail: NICU patients including preterm infants

population_detail: preterm or low-birth-weight infants (<=2300g or <=36 weeks)
intervention: three glucometers: Precision Pcx, One-Touch Verio, LifeScan SureStep Flexx
outcomes_measured: correlation coefficients overall and stratified by glucose <=60 mg/dL vs >60 mg/dL
primary_result: correlation 0.888/0.884/0.900 overall; markedly lower at <=60 mg/dL (0.674/0.687/0.679) than >60 mg/dL (0.822/0.819/0.839)

secondary_results: low sensitivity for hypoglycaemia detection despite high specificity across all three devices, in this preterm/LBW-specific population
ascertainment_method: paired POC vs laboratory analyser
directness: direct - preterm/LBW population specifically

setting: Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt
population_detail: preterm and ill neonates with umbilical arterial catheter access
intervention: blood glucose monitor (Inform II) on capillary (heel-stick) and arterial samples
comparator: YSI 2300 Stat Plus plasma glucose (arterial sample)
outcomes_measured: proportion of results meeting CLSI/FDA tolerance criteria
primary_result: arterial BGM results predominantly met CLSI/FDA criteria; capillary results markedly less reliable
effect_size: 27.5% of capillary BGM results fell outside CLSI/FDA tolerance criteria (vs low discordance for arterial)
secondary_results: discrepancy attributed to capillary sampling/perfusion factors rather than device chemistry (same device used for both sample types)
ascertainment_method: paired capillary and arterial POC vs plasma reference
directness: direct - preterm and ill neonates (explicitly addressing generalisability gap from healthy-term-only prior studies)
grade_reason: imprecision (single centre, n=40); indirectness (preterm/ill population may not generalise to the healthy late-preterm/term population BAPM's screening pathway primarily targets)
key_limitation: authors explicitly note prior BGM studies mostly included healthy-term neonates only, limiting applicability to preterm/ill infants - this study fills that gap

glucose_threshold_used: not a single threshold (CLSI/FDA tolerance criteria applied)

setting: six tertiary NICUs (Shikoku Neonatal Medical Research Group)

population_detail: inborn NICU infants in first 14 postnatal days
intervention: point-of-care (POC) testing (multiple analytes including glucose)
outcomes_measured: mean difference (CL minus POC) for glucose and other analytes
primary_result: POC systematically UNDERESTIMATED glucose vs central lab by mean 2.3 mg/dL (0.13 mmol/L)
effect_size: also underestimated sodium (6.0 mEq/L), potassium (0.1 mEq/L), chloride (5.1 mEq/L); overestimated hemoglobin/hematocrit
secondary_results: glucose and hemoglobin differences INCREASED over postnatal time; hematocrit difference remained stable
ascertainment_method: paired POC vs central laboratory (linear mixed-effects models)

directness: direct - inborn NICU infants
grade_reason: imprecision (single centre); risk of bias (retrospective, paired-timing window up to 1 hour may introduce true physiological change between samples)
key_limitation: direction of bias (underestimation) is OPPOSITE to Roth-Kleiner 2010's overestimation finding with a different device/era - genuine inconsistency, not resolved
notes: Recent (2025) evidence of systematic POC underestimation, contrasting with older overestimation findings - key evidence for the (d) tension on inconsistent bias direction across studies
gestational_age_range: NICU inborn infants, first 14 postnatal days (GA not further specified in abstract)
glucose_threshold_used: not a single threshold (mean-difference bias study)

population_detail: NICU newborns with hypoglycaemic POC results (Sept 2022-Aug 2024)

comparator: confirmatory central laboratory serum glucose (Roche cobas c501)
outcomes_measured: correlation and regression agreement between POC and serum
primary_result: significant correlation r=0.825; POC systematically higher than lab (positive bias)
effect_size: Deming regression slope 1.223, intercept -0.75; Passing-Bablok slope 1.200, intercept -0.70

ascertainment_method: paired POC vs confirmatory central lab serum
directness: direct - NICU population with confirmed hypoglycaemic readings

key_limitation: single small retrospective study; contrarian conclusion not yet replicated and in tension with BAPM's confirmation requirement and the great majority of the accuracy literature
notes: Erratum published separately at PMID 42387304 (DOI 10.1515/jpem-2026-0438), same authors/journal; central evidence for the (a)/(d) discussion of the governance/diagnosis question
gestational_age_range: NICU newborns (GA not specified in abstract)
glucose_threshold_used: not a single threshold (regression/correlation study of POC vs serum in already-hypoglycaemic range)
